label: prf:atom-knot-exists
title: Proof of atom knot exists
html:
Proof. We construct the normal form (NF) T_w \in H_{3(Z+N)}(q) explicitly.

First, we specify the intra-nucleon structure. Each Borromean baryon (borromean baryon) possesses a canonical NF in H_3(R, q) on 3 strands. Let T_p, T_n \in H_3(R, q) denote the proton and neutron NFs.

Second, we embed these into the many-body algebra. The disconnected tensor T_p^{\otimes Z} \otimes T_n^{\otimes N} \in H_3(R, q)^{\otimes (Z+N)} embeds into H_{3(Z+N)}(q) via the block-diagonal inclusion. This includes only the intra-nucleon strands.

Third, we connect the baryons. The inter-nucleon connector w_{\mathrm{inter}} \in S_{3(Z+N)} is the permutation that realizes the pp, nn, and pn crossings between adjacent baryon blocks (atomic braid crossing table).

Fourth, we assemble the product. The product T_w = T_{w_{q^Z}} \cdot T_{w_{\bar q^N}} \cdot T_{w_{\mathrm{inter}}} is a well-defined element of H_{3(Z+N)}(q). Its Markov closure \hat\beta = \hat T_w forms a closed braid in S^3.

The Diamond Lemma for the Hecke algebra (hecke normal form) guarantees that the NF remains independent of the NF-rewriting order. Thus, the constructed atom-knot is well-defined. \square
